steps.what: Choose goals, available materials and constraints for the group
Write the activity sequence and instructions

loop.input: Teacher's goals, age range, duration, materials and restrictions from the activity brief
loop.output: One proposed sequence with instructions and source goal references
loop.check: Teacher checks developmental fit, safety, feasibility and meaning in s3; rejects invented materials or assumptions
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, then teacher writes the sequence
loop.why_not_simpler: Try an existing activity template first; composing instructions for an unusual combination of goals needs language drafting

steps.what: Check and adapt the final activity to these children
Set out materials and arrange the activity space
Lead games, arts and crafts, music or storytelling for physical, mental and social development

tasks.design: Test reusable activity templates in {DOCS}, then offer bounded drafting from the teacher's activity brief where a template does not fit. The teacher checks the actual sequence and keeps all setup, live leadership and adaptation time.
tasks.previous_blocker: A goal alone does not specify the children, materials or safe activity sequence.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can combine teacher-supplied constraints without receiving pupil records.
tasks.still_hard: Judging readiness and keeping children engaged remain situated work.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher notices confusion, distress and emerging interests while leading play.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less writing before activities; teaching responsibility and decision rights stay the same.

reach.task: Review an activity against a curriculum goal

evidence.claim: Snappet offers activity drafting from a lesson goal; this supports the drafting capability, not preschool safety or these savings.
The proposed time allocation and retained checks are provisional model knowledge, not observed school timings.

assumptions: Boundary is ordinary classroom activity planning and delivery, with an existing short activity plan actually used today. Field-trip transport bookings and permission sends are separate event work and receive no saving here.

The teacher supplies goal code, age range, group size, duration, available materials and restrictions in s1; no clean feed or pupil inference is assumed. Missing fields are entered manually in that retained step.

The ten writing hours contain five hours of assembling instructions and five of editing and individual adaptation. The separate five-hour final suitability check remains fully counted; ordinary document save time stays within writing without a gate.
Use native templates before custom drafting. No automatic activity publication or pupil assessment is proposed.
unknowns: Whether usable activity plans are already available
Actual planning versus live activity time
research_questions: Can teachers use existing templates without drafting?
Which generated instructions require a full rewrite for preschool use?

already_counted.description: Editing the draft and checking suitability

incremental.description: Maintain allowed materials and activity templates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is 5 hours less 0.8 upkeep = 4.2. Cautious case: bespoke activities require all ten writing hours or existing plans already remove assembly; retain all work and do not deploy the added tool, saving zero. No teaching or setup time is cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notice concerns and discuss appropriate support

steps.what: Notice and investigate concerning signs during everyday activity
Write the factual concern in the pupil records system {OTHER}
Save the concern note in the same pupil record
Read relevant previous observations and support context
Discuss the concern and next action with the supervisor
Discuss observations with parents or guardians and hear their context
Discuss specialist concerns and agree appropriate follow-up within the teacher's role

tasks.design: Configure the pupil records system {OTHER} to show existing factual observations and support context together. Concern capture, interpretation and conversations remain with the teacher, with no automated diagnosis or emotion inference.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant factual history may require navigating several record sections.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record views can expose selected existing fields without classifying children.
tasks.still_hard: A worrying sign can have many explanations and needs careful discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Trust and contextual understanding determine how concerns are raised.
tasks.altitude: One small navigation reduction; responsibility for identifying and discussing concerns is unchanged.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys supports pupil records and learning-goal tracking; this does not establish an automated concern detector.
A configured record view may remove repeated navigation while retaining all reading and discussion; the estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal teacher's boundary includes first factual concern capture and three kinds of discussion. The 6470 routine performance observation note is a different artefact; a concern already recorded there is reused, never entered twice for roll-up credit.

Existing pupil history contains dated author-attributed observations, current support actions and access rights maintained by the recording staff. No inferred labels or external medical feed is assumed; absent history is sought manually within s4.

Only one of ten context-reading hours is repeated screen navigation; nine remain for reading, comparison and clarification. Concern writing and its one-hour ordinary save remain fully retained and ungated.

These are live conversations, with no automatic written disclosure or external send. If a formal referral is required, its actual preparation, permission check and send must be separately measured before extending this design.
unknowns: Whether current pupil views already show the relevant context
Which discussions require a formal written referral
research_questions: Does navigation actually consume time beyond reading the concern history?

already_counted.description: Read and interpret existing history including missing-history follow-up

incremental.description: Review view fields and access when record structure changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 1 navigation hour less 0.2 upkeep = 0.8. If the history already appears together, or relevant context is held outside the pupil system, all ten context hours remain and the extra view is not deployed, giving zero. Identification, note capture, save and discussions receive no cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain complete and accurate pupil records

steps.what: Check which pupil record fields and updates are required
Read existing observations and verify incoming record updates
Capture new parent-supplied changes in the pupil records system {OTHER}
Copy existing pupil identifiers and dates into required record sections
Check completeness and resolve contradictory or missing information
Verify meaning, attribution and accuracy against the original sources
Save the maintained pupil record

tasks.design: Use native linked pupil fields and completeness rules in the pupil records system {OTHER}. The teacher captures incoming changes, resolves discrepancies and checks the actual meaning; ordinary same-system saving remains unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Record sections may repeat identifiers and require manual completeness checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked fields and required-field validation can remove exact repetition without interpreting development.
tasks.still_hard: Contradictory parent information and ambiguous observations need human verification.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher knows what an observation establishes and what remains uncertain.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat entry, with the same responsibility for record accuracy and access.

reach.task: Define a usable pupil record template
reach.learn: Field provenance, minimum necessary data and exception handling

evidence.claim: ParnasSys offers pupil records and learning-goal tracking. Native linked-field feasibility still needs checking locally.
Exact field reuse and deterministic completeness checks can reduce repeat entry; the proposed allocation is model knowledge, not a measured school baseline.

assumptions: Boundary is maintaining actual required pupil records, not producing a new report or submission. Original routine observation capture belongs to 6470 and first concern capture to 6471; this task reads those existing notes without claiming their creation again.

Recording teachers supply pupil ID, observation date, author and source-note ID. Parents supply actual new contact or factual updates; reading and verifying them is s2 and first capture is fully priced in s3. Missing or unstructured input is handled manually, not provided by a free extraction feed.

The school supplies its applicable field list; no universal national requirement is invented. Test native links first. The 15 repeat-entry hours concern exact identifiers and dates, not copying free-text conclusions or saving the author's work.

Of twenty completeness hours, five are repetitive empty-field and date-format checks; fifteen remain for resolving missing or contradictory information. Final semantic verification is separately retained in s6. No external disclosure or consequential submission is automated.
unknowns: Whether these repeated fields exist in today's record workflow
Which required fields already validate automatically
Whether linked identifiers can be configured safely
research_questions: Can a sample record be maintained with native links while preserving source attribution?
How much completeness time concerns missing-field detection versus contacting people?

already_counted.description: Resolve completeness exceptions and verify meaning against sources

incremental.description: Maintain field mappings and required-field rules

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is 15 exact-repeat hours plus 5 mechanical check hours, less 2 upkeep = 18. Cautious case: legacy sections cannot share fields, so all fifteen entry hours remain; required-field checking alone removes five, less two upkeep = 3. All source capture and the ordinary one-hour save remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe and evaluate children's development and health

steps.what: Observe children's activity, interaction and physical wellbeing
Evaluate observations against developmental context and previous performance
Enter the factual observation and evaluation in pupil records {OTHER}
Save the observation note in the same pupil record

tasks.design: Keep observation and developmental evaluation with the teacher. Configure only current-pupil identity, author and date defaults in the pupil records system {OTHER}, retaining all factual writing and ordinary saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some note forms require repeated identity headers despite an already selected pupil.
tasks.enabler_now: Native form defaults can reuse the current record context without assessing a child.
tasks.still_hard: Separating a passing variation from a meaningful pattern depends on context and repeated observation.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher connects behaviour with the child's circumstances without reducing it to a score.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in repeated headers; evaluation rights and live workload do not change.

reach.learn: Factual observation, uncertainty and contextual interpretation

evidence.claim: Native record defaults may avoid repeated identity entry while preserving all observation and interpretation; this is model knowledge and not a measured saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes the actual first routine observation note read later during record maintenance in 6482. A new concern note in 6471 is distinct; if the same note serves both tasks it has one owner and no second saving.

The teacher supplies actual observation, context and evaluation in s3. Selected pupil ID comes from the current record; author comes from authenticated identity and date from a visible clock value. Teacher corrects all defaults in the retained writing time; absent context means manual headers.

Only 0.95 of nineteen note-entry hours is repeat headers; 18.05 remains for first capture, phrasing and checking. The one-hour same-system author save is unchanged with no approval stage. No automated pupil evaluation, diagnosis, surveillance or new observation log is proposed.
unknowns: Whether records are entered directly or first on paper
research_questions: Does the present observation form contain any repeated header entry to remove?

already_counted.description: Capture and check the complete observation and evaluation

incremental.description: Check defaults after pupil-record form changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 0.95 header hours less 0.2 upkeep = 0.75. If current forms already default the header, or paper capture cannot reuse the selected pupil context, retain all nineteen entry hours and do not add the configuration, yielding zero. Neither observation nor evaluation is shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Teaching, observation and sensitive conversations remain central. The practical change is less repeated record entry and some help composing activity instructions.
reach: Work with an instructional coordinator on useful activity templates and record fields
skills_to_grow: Check generated instructions against real developmental needs
Maintain clear source attribution in pupil records
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends less time repeating record headers while keeping responsibility for children's development and relationships.
